title: Cook one recipe together, start to finish
description: One recipe, two cooks, no phones at the table. Pick something neither of you has mastered, divide the jobs, and eat whatever the experiment produces.
author: SparkKindly · AI-assisted

body.heading: Choose the recipe fairly
paragraphs: Pick a dish that is new to both cooks — or at least new enough that neither gets to be the boss. Something with real jobs in it: dough to knead, vegetables to chop, a sauce that needs watching. One-pot wonders and flatbreads are perfect first collaborations.
Read the whole recipe aloud together before touching an ingredient. Most kitchen disasters are just surprises that a two-minute read would have prevented.

body.heading: Divide, don't duplicate
paragraphs: Split the jobs by task, not by seniority: one cook chops while the other stirs; one washes as the other plates. Agree who is in charge of the oven and the sharp knives, and let the cook who is not seasoning get the casting vote on salt.
Talk while you work — that is the point of the exercise. Cooking side by side produces the kind of conversation that sitting face to face often doesn't.

body.heading: Eat the evidence
paragraphs: Serve whatever comes out, exactly as it is, and eat it together at a table. Review it like friendly critics: what worked, what was odd, what you would change. Write the verdict on the recipe itself, in pencil.
The dish is the excuse. A shared hour, a small shared risk, and a meal that exists only because two people made it — that is the actual recipe.

takeaway: One new recipe, jobs divided fairly, verdict written in pencil: the dish is the excuse, the hour together is the meal.
materials: One recipe, printed or written out
Its ingredients, checked before you start
supervision: An adult leads on sharp knives, hot pans and the oven throughout; children help with washing, measuring, mixing and tearing.
safetyNotes: Wash hands before cooking and tie back long hair and loose sleeves.
Keep pan handles turned inwards, and treat every hot dish as guilty until proven cool.
Check allergies for everyone who will eat, before choosing the recipe.
